programme.title: Sensitive Content
programme.desc: What defines "sensitive content" in an age of constant information flow? This thought-provoking documentary delves into the complex world of graphic imagery, difficult truths, and the ethics of visibility. Through interviews with journalists, content moderators, and experts, it explores how such material is handled, who decides what is shown, and the psychological impact on both creators and audiences. Balancing awareness with responsibility, the film challenges viewers to reflect on their own role in consuming and sharing powerful, often unsettling content.

programme.title: At Dawn
programme.desc: At Dawn is an atmospheric one-off documentary that explores the powerful symbolism of daybreak. As the first light touches different landscapes and lives, the film captures moments of silence, movement, and emotional transformation. With a calm visual style and reflective narrative, it looks at how a new day can represent hope, memory, resilience, and renewal. The documentary invites viewers to slow down and observe the world in its most delicate and meaningful hours.

programme.title: A Game Where Children Fight
programme.desc: This investigative documentary exposes the systematic militarisation of Ukrainian children in temporarily occupied territories, where occupying forces threaten parents into sending them to Russian schools and youth organisations. Through the story of Oksana, who was deceived into attending Russia's Avangard camp, the film shows how military instructors at the Voin centre teach teenagers to operate drones and handle firearms and grenades. Journalists also identify the organisers of a system designed to prepare a new generation of Ukrainians for endless war.
